correctness.rationale: Embed the basis e_i as t^i in the associative cyclic group algebra B=k[t]/(t^p−1)=k[u]/u^p, and check e_i⋆e_j=t^{(1−λ)i+λj}=σ_{1−λ}(t^i)σ_λ(t^j). Every ⋆-idempotent has augmentation zero or one. If zero it lies successively in I^{2^r} and vanishes. Augmentation-one elements are 1+I, and truncated characteristic-p log/exp polynomials are inverse abelian group maps because I^p=0 and coefficients below degree p are units. For v=log t, σ_c(v^j)=c^j v^j; linearized idempotency equation restricts coefficients exactly to J. For two idempotents, log of their ⋆-product is σ_a(H)+σ_b(K), yielding the affine quandle law with nonzero coefficients summing to one in each coordinate. Direct exhaustive bilinear product enumeration over F3 and F5 confirms counts; independently checked resonances for seven primes up to31.
residual_risks: The log/exp argument is performed only inside auxiliary associative nilpotent B; the original quandle algebra is not associative.
The coefficient field characteristic must equal the prime base-quandle order; no extension to composite order or other characteristic.
